Backstory: My buddy and I have always been gamers growing up in the age of the Nes as our first video games systems.

Recently we have been at a debate of the future of Consoles and PC gaming. I stand on the side of the fence of the Steam Box purposed direction: Where one day you will have a PC powerful enough to host games on eight different Televisions in your house.

He stands on the side where he believes after this generation there will be no more need for a console and Microsoft’s Xbox Live, Sony’s PlayStation Plus and the other respective game services will be all online streaming games from their services. Convinced by his experience with Playstation Now, he believes in this future.

I on the other hand expect gaming to still be a system taxing product and expect machines to come out that are even more powerful, but not in the vein of console. I see the next iteration of consoles, more in line with the PC and expect upgradable Consoles from the next gen if not just well crafted PC’s.

Both our visions will manifest in some way shape or form, since they are based of the current trends. What does this Subverse think about the topic?

edit:grammar
What do you envision is the future of Consoles/Dedicated PC gaming Devices?

Nintedo will continue making consoles. Sony will go bankrupt. Microsoft will discontinue the XBox brand.

You will own a nintendo console, or you will have a "Living Room PC" for gaming.

There is very unlikely to be another new console that doesn't have the nintendo brand on it. We've been seing it for years. Everyone else is interested in making multi-entertainment platforms (which are really just shitty PCs when you boil it down.) Nintendo is the only company that still knows what a game console is.

You put a game in it, you play it. No installing, there arn't endless patches and firmware updates, the non-game features are in the background out of the way.

Streaming may be the future, but it will be more in the style of steam, than Playstation Now.

I honesty don't think we'll see a cloud "console" any time soon. Playstation Now is still in beta so i guess we'll see how that plays out. Their pricing scheme is far from optimal though and the ping/delay will be a major factor.

I think the idea of consoles evolving to allow for upgrades is an interesting prospect, but I don't know if I see it happening. Consoles seem to try to distance themselves from PC gaming on that end by releasing upgraded versions (at least in my perspective) which allows for more money. Delving into the world where they have the opportunity to upgrade might be off-putting for console gamers, as what would make that any different from PC gaming at that point?

The movement toward online gaming and streaming games is one I see happening, but again, I think would be difficult to implement. Internet is still a huge factor and was PrivateJoker mentioned, ping/delay would be a huge factor.

I think ultimately the console trend will remain the same - Nintendo will continue as they do, making consoles, and Microsoft and Sony will continue trying to integrate all these other features into it. This is nice, but really, much of which can already be accomplished with a PC.
